brand.beakbound.note: Latin letters, never translated. Suffixes with an apostrophe: Beakbound'u.

char.pip.note: Name kept. Suffixes after an apostrophe: Pip'in, Pip'e.

char.peaches.note: Name kept (said "Piçız"); suffixes follow the sound: Peaches'in, Peaches'e. Her own peach puns use "şeftali".

char.minty.note: Name kept: Minty'nin, Minty'ye. The mint flavour is "nane" (never the name).

char.postmaster-bill.note: "Postacıbaşı" = head postman, a warm old-fashioned title that also works alone ("Postacıbaşının emri"). Bill'in, Bill'e.

char.courier.note: Epicene, fits all four birds; "Kurye Pip", "Kraliyet Kuryesi". "postacı" is kept for "postman"/"postie".

char.narrator.note: Never named on screen; captions use sen ("İlk günün.").

boss.baron-bat.note: Order as in "Kont Drakula"; short form and address "Baron" (Baron'un).

boss.spitter-king.note: "tükürükçü" = the one who spits, same word as the beetles; Bill and the birds say "Kral".

boss.dusk-empress.note: "alacakaranlık" = dusk/twilight, same word as her moths; short form and address "İmparatoriçe". UI: the boss-name keys have a 20-character budget (28 needed), so every UI place (name card, health bar context, level 3-8 name, thank-you signer, defeat banner, store) uses "Akşam İmparatoriçesi" (bar name "İMPARATORİÇE", builder key "Akşam"). Voice keeps the full name (story before-3-1-2, flight pip-boss-empress-01): owner to decide whether to align.

boss.pirate-captain.note: Short form and address "Kaptan"; he calls himself "Kaptan" (Kaptan'ın).

boss.ember-dragon.note: "kor" = glowing ember, same root as "korlar" (attack.embers); short form and address "Ejderha".

guardian.king-coo.note: "gu gu" is how Turkish writes a pigeon's coo; short, card-friendly, King Kong rhythm. His card shout "COO!" = "GUU!".

guardian.searchlight-gargoyle.note: "ışıldak" = searchlight; splits as small IŞILDAKLI over big GARGOYL. Short form "Gargoyl" ("Gargoyl kabul ediyor.").

npc.sloth-stargazer.note: "tembel hayvan" = sloth; the cargo tag shortens to "Tembel hayvana".

npc.samba-macaws.note: Macaw = ara papağanı; "papağan" is enough and kid-clear.

npc.drum-captain.note: Band-leader word, never "kaptan" (that is the pirate).

npc.chariot-racers.note: Roman chariot racing is "araba yarışı" in Turkish; short for the tag.

npc.pyramid-caretaker.note: Feminine by the voice only (Turkish has no gender).

npc.caravan-leader.note: The exact Turkish word for a caravan leader.

npc.baker.note: The Paris baker (3-7); the 4-2 one is "yanardağ fırıncısı".

npc.ferry-crew.note: "tayfa" is kept for the pirate crew.

npc.sphinx.note: Turkish name of the Sphinx (Sfenks'e, Sfenks'in); Peaches: "Sfenks Bey".

npc.unit-7.note: "birim" = unit; reads as a robot designation.

npc.parrot.note: Capitalised when the Captain addresses it as a name.

title.postmaster.note: Head postman, old-fashioned and warm; also alone ("Postacıbaşının emri").

title.keeper-of-the-twilight-veil.note: "tül" = her silk veil, same word as the fight hints.

title.terror-of-the-high-tide.note: High tide = "kabaran sular" (clearer for kids than "met").

title.keeper-of-lost-letters.note: Plural job title; echoes his card epithet.

title.royal-courier.note: Same "kurye" as the courier, for Pip's "Ben sadece kuryeyim. Kurye Pip."

title.commissioner-of-the-curb.note: "kaldırım" = the curb where pigeons peck; K-K alliteration.

title.commissioner.note: Third person: "Komiser kabul ediyor."; addressed as "Komiserim" (the natural Turkish address to a police chief).

region.ancient-arabia.note: Storybook Arabia, parallel with Antik Roma.

region.cyberpunk-city.note: Turkish spelling of the genre; Bill says "neon şehir".

place.city-of-light.note: The established Turkish epithet of Paris.

place.sugarloaf-mountain.note: Literal rendering of Pão de Açúcar; keeps "şeker" so Pip's sugar joke works.

place.theatre-marquee.note: The lit awning over the theatre door; King Coo: "Tentenin altındaymış."

place.canopy.note: The roof of leaves; same words as the chapter.

chapter.lamplight-line.note: "hat" = a transport/delivery line; keeps the lamp image (the L-L alliteration does not carry over).

chapter.edge-of-the-map.note: Same words as the place and the achievement.

level.2-5.note: Coined like Skyfall: the sky falling down; shouted as "Gök çöküyor!".

level.2-6.note: The official postal formula, as his catchphrase.

level.3-2.note: Film-title ring (cf. "Yağmur Altında"); keeps wheels + rain.

level.3-4.note: Same words as the Gargoyle's headline.

level.3-7.note: Adapted: NOT "Geceyarısı Ekspresi", a film title that is notorious and painful in Turkey; midnight + post keeps the idea.

level.4-4.note: Low water = the receding sea; pairs with 4-5.

level.4-5.note: Nautical highest tide (not spring the season) = the swelling sea; pairs with 4-4 and "KABARAN SULARIN DEHŞETİ".

level.5-5.note: "silüet" = city skyline; same "sprint" as the button.

level.5-6.note: The usual Turkish name of the Lantern Festival.

level.5-7.note: Turkish idiom for the last stage of a journey.

level.starter-stair-squats.note: Squat = "çömelme" as in "Çömel ve Uç". UI 2026-10-07: was "Merdiven Çömelmeleri". "Merdiven Çömelmeleri" (20) does not fit the 16-character starter card. Not spoken.

cargo.1-1.en: A birthday card for the toucan twins

cargo.1-2.en: Star charts for the sloth stargazer
cargo.1-2.note: Shortened from "yıldız gözlemcisi tembel hayvana" for the 40-character tag.

cargo.1-4.en: Feather boas for the carnival parade

cargo.1-5.en: A rush invitation for the drum captain

cargo.1-6.en: Cocoa beans for the temple cooks

cargo.1-7.en: A sundial for the dawn keeper

cargo.1-8.en: A final notice for Baron Bat

cargo.2-1.en: Laurel wreaths for the chariot racers

cargo.2-2.en: A new chisel for the statue carver

cargo.2-3.en: Water buckets for the fire brigade

cargo.2-4.en: A book of new riddles for the Sphinx

cargo.2-5.en: A telescope for the pyramid astronomer

cargo.2-6.en: A feather duster for the caretaker

cargo.2-7.en: Lamp oil for the lantern sellers

cargo.2-8.en: Water flasks for the long caravan

cargo.2-9.en: A stop-brewing order for the Spitter King
cargo.2-9.note: A stop-brewing order = a boiling ban.

cargo.3-1.en: Light bulbs for the theatre marquee

cargo.3-3.en: Hot pretzels for the night-shift cabbies
cargo.3-3.note: "pretzel" is known in Turkey; "simit" is taken by King Coo's bagel.

cargo.3-4.en: A weather vane for the tallest tower

cargo.3-6.en: Sheet music for the accordion player

cargo.3-7.en: A midnight love letter for the baker

cargo.3-8.en: A wake-up call for the Dusk Empress
cargo.3-8.note: "uyandırma servisi" = a hotel wake-up call (literal) and, jokingly, a warning.

cargo.4-1.en: A new lens for the lighthouse keeper

cargo.4-2.en: Oven mitts for the volcano baker

cargo.4-3.en: Kite string for the beach festival

cargo.4-4.en: A reply for the island hermit

cargo.4-5.en: A tide table for the ferry crew

cargo.4-6.en: Fish biscuits for the gull colony

cargo.4-7.en: Dry socks for the storm-watch sailors

cargo.4-8.en: A return-the-mail order for the Captain

cargo.5-1.en: Woolly hats for the penguin choir

cargo.5-2.en: Hot cocoa for the polar station

cargo.5-3.en: Spare fuses for the noodle bar sign

cargo.5-4.en: A paper letter for a curious robot

cargo.5-5.en: Race tickets for the rooftop runners

cargo.5-8.en: The first letter ever sent to the Dragon

enemy.dusk-moth.note: Same "alacakaranlık" as the Empress. "güve" is the plain moth word ("gece kelebeği" avoided: it has an adult slang sense).

enemy.straggler.note: UI says "geri döner" (comes back), as for the ankh.

enemy.brood.note: He calls them "minik böceklerim" ("bok böceği", the dung-beetle word for scarab, is avoided).

attack.screech.note: Same "çığlık" as Bill's "Çığlık atan yarasa ısırmaz".

attack.mail-call.note: A fussy postman's announcement, used as his battle cry and tag.

attack.ankh.note: The Egyptian "hayat anahtarı"; suffixes after an apostrophe (ankh'tan).

hazard.steam-geyser.note: Hot = "sıcak", soft = "yumuşak"; hop = "üstünden atla", ride = "üstüne bin".

hazard.tide.note: The surge is "sular kabarıyor"; HIGH TIDE = "KABARAN SULAR".

set-piece.rush-path.note: A sudden rush of danger; HUD "AKIN ×2!".

set-piece.gale.note: A sudden storm wind; distinct from "fırtına" (storm).

weapon.shoot.note: Button label; in sentences "vur" / "ateş et" ("Tohumları vurup düşür", "sen de ateş et!").

weapon.sprint.note: Sports loanword in everyday use ("sprint atmak").

ui.sky-club-post.note: Also the door greeting "Gök Kulübü Postası!".

ui.passport-stamp.note: Ink/visa stamp; the Captain's postage stamps are "pul" (two words, as in Turkish).

ui.star-marks.note: "çentik" = notch on the bar; Pip: "İlk çentik yandı!".

ui.trail-stardust-sparkles.note: UI 2026-10-07: was "Yıldız tozu pırıltıları". Singular to fit the 22-character chip. Not spoken.

ui.special-delivery.note: Same words in the achievement and the voice lines.

ui.sky-reclaimed.note: UI 2026-10-07: was "GÖKYÜZÜ GERİ ALINDI". "GÖKYÜZÜ GERİ ALINDI" (19) does not fit 18. Not spoken.

ui.bonk.note: Turkish cartoon bump; also the Empress's "Küt. Küt."

ui.splash.note: Turkish sound of falling into water.

ui.to-be-continued.note: Exact caption used by the narrator: "Devam edecek… Sıradaki durak: Paris, Işıklar Şehri."

ui.camera-lab.note: UI 2026-10-07: was "Kamera ve takip laboratuvarı". "laboratuvarı" does not fit the 24-character Settings key; the lab screen says "KAMERA TESTİ". Not spoken.

ui.play-games.note: Google's Turkish product name is "Google Play Oyunlar". UI 2026-10-07: was "Play Games". Google's own Turkish name, as the UI key asks ("Play Oyunlar'a bağlan"). Not spoken.

achievement.on-the-dot.note: Turkish idiom of precision ("tam on ikiden vurmak").

achievement.all-rounder.note: Idiom "her telden çalmak" = good at everything.

achievement.out-of-the-spotlight.note: Both his searchlight and a ham losing the spotlight.

achievement.lamplighter.note: The old job of lighting street lamps.

story.warm-letter.note: "sıcak" is both warm and kind, as in English.

story.pigeonholes.note: Adapted pun: "Postanemizde bugüne dek tek bir posta güvercini olmadı." (a post office that never had a carrier pigeon).

story.bread-cart.note: Localised: the Turkish street bread cart, so it pairs with the simit pay.

story.bagel.note: Localised: simit is the Turkish bagel, warmer and funnier for Turkish kids.

story.mint-tea.note: Minty's name has no link to "nane"; his joke becomes "Tıpkı benim gibi ferah!".

story.letter-phrases.note: Turkish letter opener and postcard cliché; flight recipe adds “Geçmiş olsun” and “Sevgilerle”.

story.first-letter.en: the first letter ever sent to the Dragon

story.dotted-i.en: He dotted his “i” with a tiny bat.
story.dotted-i.target: “i” harfinin noktasına minik bir yarasa çizdi.
story.dotted-i.note: Turkish has the dotted i, so the joke works as is.

story.headwear.note: Each item plainly: taç, şişe taç, kep, şapka.

motto.every-letter-lands.note: "yerini bulmak" = to reach the place it belongs (also said of a well-aimed shot or a welcome gift). Dragon: "Her mektup gerçekten yerini bulur mu?"; Minty: "…benimki HIZLA bulur!"

motto.every-letter-delivered.note: Echoes the motto with "teslim". UI 2026-10-07: was "Her mektup teslim". Full sentence on the Home campaign key (homeCampaignDone). Not spoken.

address.darling.note: Gargoyle and Peaches; the posh Baron says "azizim" instead (old-fashioned aristocratic "my dear").

address.sprat.note: The iconic tiny Black Sea fish.

address.fledgling.note: A fussy old official's word for a novice, with siz.

address.stoneface.note: Common Turkish nickname for a stony face.

address.commissioner.note: The natural Turkish address to a police chief.

address.her-highness.note: Pip's grand, old-fashioned title for the Empress.

address.peaches-pet-names.note: Set used, never repeated in a row: şekerim, tatlım, canım, cicim, bal küpüm, lokumum, bal böceğim, pamuk şekerim, kuzucuğum (all gender-neutral).

address.minions.en: Cousins! / my lovelies / my little scarabs / me hearties
address.minions.note: Plural address in each boss's own voice.

phrase.baron-bat-line.en: This route is my roost now, little courier!
phrase.baron-bat-line.target: Bu rota artık benim tüneğim, küçük kurye!

phrase.spitter-king-line.en: Every letter on my road goes in the brew!

phrase.dusk-empress-line.en: Hush now. The night mail is sleeping.

phrase.pirate-captain-line.en: Arr! Every mailbag on these waves be mine!
phrase.pirate-captain-line.target: Arrr! Bu dalgalardaki her posta çantası benimdir!
phrase.pirate-captain-line.note: "-dir" gives the old-salt ring of "be mine".

phrase.ember-dragon-line.en: The sky is mine. Your letters are kindling.

phrase.neferhoo-line.en: Return to sender! This route has a courier.
phrase.neferhoo-line.target: Göndericiye iade! Bu rotanın kuryesi var.

phrase.king-coo-line.en: Nobody flies till the bread cart is found!
phrase.king-coo-line.target: Simit arabası bulunana dek kimse uçmayacak!

phrase.searchlight-gargoyle-line.en: Hold still! Nobody ever stays in the light.

phrase.return-to-sender.note: The Turkish post's formula for returned mail.

phrase.signed-sealed-delivered.note: Three beats; Minty swaps the last: "…vınnn!".

phrase.peaches-tagline.en: Rosy cheeks, curly crest, all heart.
phrase.peaches-tagline.target: Al yanaklar, kıvırcık tepe, kocaman yürek.

phrase.minty-tagline.en: Tiny hummer. Fresh sprig. Full speed.
phrase.minty-tagline.target: Minik sinekkuşu. Taze nane. Tam gaz.

phrase.orbit-tagline.en: A dreamy owl who flies by starlight.
phrase.orbit-tagline.target: Yıldız ışığında uçan hayalperest bir baykuş.

phrase.sprint-bye-bye-gravity.note: "güle güle" is what you say to the one leaving.

phrase.keep-your-beak-up.note: From "başını dik tut" (keep your head up).

phrase.all-screech.note: From the proverb "Havlayan köpek ısırmaz" (barking dogs don't bite).

phrase.no-flame-seal.en: No flame seal on this guardian.

phrase.at-your-disservice.note: Mirror of "hizmetinizde" (at your service): "Baron Yarasa, hizmetsizliğinizde."

phrase.sticks-and-stones.note: Twist of "Söz uçar, yazı kalır" keeping the stone joke.

phrase.pirate-speak.note: Turkish stage-pirate kit: "Arrr!", "Ahoy!", "Dur bakalım!", "Hay gemimin direği!", "tayfa", "be", "-dir" endings.

phrase.welcome-to-the-club.note: Same idiom in Turkish; Bill to the Gargoyle with siz: "Kulübe hoş geldiniz".

ui.home.note: Every "Home" key and "back home" label ("Ana menüye dön").

ui.switch-on-off.note: 4-character budget: "KAPALI" does not fit; "AÇIK/KAPALI" if the budget grows to 6.

ui.shoot-key.note: "Ateş tuşuna dokun", "Ateş'i basılı tut" (apostrophe after the key name).

ui.seconds-unit.note: "{n} sn"; compact HUD forms "12sn"; "s" only in replayMagnet (14 characters).

ui.out-of.note: Avoids a suffix on the number: "3 üzerinden 2 yıldız".

ui.level-builder-short.note: Short form of "Seviye Atölyesi"; the editor is "düzenleyici".

ui.to-medal.note: Dative of the medal words on the passport bar.

ui.needs-a-moment.note: Load-error headings: "Harita biraz zaman istiyor.", "Yuvan biraz zaman istiyor."

ui.vs.note: Caption "Pip – Minty"; result "Pip, Minty'yi yendi" (select on Minty for the buffer y).
